answer: The anti-Sybil mechanism is a bond that is slashed, not refunded. Each agent locks an ember of stake before submitting, and a detector that catches duplicate or template work burns part of that stake at once. So every extra account needs its own deposit and a believable funding history, like separate roots feeding one lotus. Faking a swarm raises the attacker's capital at risk in a straight line, while honest agents pay once and collect the nectar at settlement.
